Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery — Skylark Health (recap & next steps)

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call so the whole team (Ben, Priyom) is aligned and we can move to a pilot proposal. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level pain points you described:
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak billing cycles (black-friday-like spikes for claims ingestion).
- Current inference costs and ops complexity from maintaining several single-GPU services across GCP projects.
- Need for strict data isolation and auditability for PHI workflows (SOC2 + HIPAA considerations).

Current stack & constraints you mentioned:
- Self-hosted inference on GCP (custom orchestration) using an instruction-tuned open model; each service runs on one A2-equivalent instance (no pooling).
- Typical steady traffic: ~100 requests/sec (p95 latency target today ~250ms).
- Short bursts up to ~350 req/s that last ~20–45 minutes (weekly batch windows).
- KV cache and session affinity are used in your current pipeline (long context retrievals).

Success criteria for Dedicated fit (what you want this pilot to prove):
1) Predictable throughput: sustained 100 req/s with ability to handle 3x burst to 350 req/s without >2x latency degradation.
2) Isolation: tenant-level network/isolation and audit logs that satisfy your security team.
3) Cost target: total token cost and infra run-rate <= current monthly spend + 15% while improving latency.
4) SLOs: p95 generation latency <150ms for common short prompts, 99.9% availability during pilot window.

Operational asks / constraints:
- Procurement timeline: target contract by end of Q3 (you said procurement can do standard PO).
- Security: you will need a completed security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence during evaluation.
- Model compatibility: want to test both the open model you use and a smaller quantized variant for cache-heavy traffic.

Proposed next steps (we’ll take these on from Redwood side):
- I: Share a proposed reserved-pool config and cost estimate for a two-week pilot (we recommend a 4x-reserved-GPU pool with burst headroom; exact instance class to be validated by Priyom). Attached: "skylark-workload-sample.csv" (you sent) and our "redwood-dedicated-checklist.pdf".
- II: Schedule a 60-minute tech deep dive with your infra engineer (propose Tue/Jul 6, 10am PT) to validate KV cache behavior and autoscale signals.
- III: Provide SOC2 artifact links and a brief security onboarding checklist.

If that looks right, we’ll draft a pilot statement of work (SOW) + measurables: throughput curves, tail-latency charts, cost per 1k tokens, and isolation verification steps.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Ava — this is a great summary and captures everything. A couple clarifications from my side:

- Burst shape: the 350 req/s spikes are driven by our nightly reconciliation job + ad-hoc customer replays; often the first 10 minutes of the window are the most intense.
- Security: SOC2 is must-have; we’ll need the actual artifact and a contact for your compliance lead.
- Procurement: we can move to a PO but need a clear pilot period and acceptance criteria. Ideally a 14-day pilot that demonstrates both steady-state and at least one scheduled spike.

We're available for the tech deep dive on Tue/Jul 6 10am PT. I’ll invite our infra lead (Rita) to the calendar invite — she’ll provide the live traffic reproducer.

On timing: procurement wants a short-term pilot SOW to approve the PO. If you can share the draft SOW and the pool config by Mon/Jul 5, that would help.

Appreciate it —
Liam O'Neal
VP, Platform Engineering | Skylark Health
liam@skylarkhealth.com
